      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

Det tilsvarer over 37 milliarder norske kroner, og spillet forbigår dermed superheltfilmen «Avengers: End Game» som den største underholdningslanseringen noensinne.

    <item>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

There was no way of knowing, back when Dane Anson was wearing a Batman cape while riding his pony in Nanaimo, how far his love of horses would take him.

]]>

There was no way of knowing, back when Dane Anson was wearing a Batman cape while riding his pony in Nanaimo, how far his love of horses would take him.

Just a few years later, he is taking on the best in the world.

“It’s a dream come true because I’ve loved horses all my life. I remember going to rodeos and wearing my cowboy costume and my love for horses already at that young age,” Anson told CHEK News.

That bond with horses is making the once shy Nanaimo teenager an international force in the hyper competitive hunter jumper ring, and he has become a top equitation rider, winning events across the U.S. and Canada. Most recently he won Overall Leading Equitation Rider honours at the 2026 Marshall+Sterling/USHJA National Championships in Las Vegas, and became the first Canadian athlete to win the Gladstone Cup.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

 “It’s definitely where I’m happiest and I wouldn’t change it for the world,” said Anson.

Since discovering his love of horses at the age of seven, his dad Rob Anson says he has hardly wanted to come down since.

“It’s pretty special to see the growth and development of Dane over the years, as we share the passion that he has for the animals, and the trust,” said Rob Anson. 

The Anson family now splits their year between Canada and the U.S. on the show circuit, as he wins championships he once only dreamed of. 

“It’s definitely a cool feeling. It’s such a rare sport and it’s not often that you get to compete with a living animal and form bonds,” said Dane Anson.

In addition, horses have helped Anson overcome once crippling anxiety. So he wants to show others that pushing yourself despite fear, can be done.

“I definitely want to do the high level jumping, and get to the top of the sport,” said Dane Anson.

“Dane used to have terrible anxiety as well as a little boy, but being able to find the confidence and the passion, within the animals to put himself out there on the big stage and be judged if you will, is something that I never would have believed that he would have been up for,” said Rob.

As this teen jumps over obstacles, that once stood in his way, to enjoy the ride of his life.

]]> 1362756 ‘Frustrating’: 2nd major cleanup of illegal dumping in a year near Qualicum https://cheknews.ca/frustrating-2nd-major-cleanup-of-illegal-dumping-in-a-year-near-qualicum-1363195/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 01:53:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363195

The items that were dumped illegally range from a boat and car to tires and a catalytic converter.

The post ‘Frustrating’: 2nd major cleanup of illegal dumping in a year near Qualicum appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The items that were dumped illegally range from a boat and car to tires and a catalytic converter.

Those things and a range of other garbage was brought out of the woods north of Qualicum Beach Saturday.

“It is frustrating. We were out here last year doing a massive clean up and we’re back at it again cleaning up similar volumes of dumped debris and whatnot,” said Four Wheel Drive Association of BC volunteer Chris Hillsden.

This was the second time in a year the Four Wheel Drive Association of BC has been to this location along Claymore Road.

Last year the group pulled out 70,000 pounds of garbage.

“It’s scattered across a fairly large area so right here on the southern outreaches of the cleanup area and it stretches for another 15 kilometres behind me,” explained 4wdabc Vancouver Island representative Colin Stuart.

He said while there are many reasons why people might dump their trash in the woods it likely comes down to avoiding paying fees at the landfill.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“Dumping illegally, household debris, you see a lot of contractor stuff like undercutting jobs usually dumping shingles and building materials out here,” added Stuart.

“I was just walking down the trails and saw all these tires and stuff and oil jugs so obviously it’s from someone’s garage or something and they don’t want to recycle them properly,” said volunteer Sam Heibein.

For every reason someone might have to come out here and dump illegally, others have their own reasons to come out and pick up after them.

“Everyone we have around us are like-minded and would prefer to see our forests clean,” said volunteer Liam Churchill.

“I’ve lived on Vancouver Island my entire life, I’ve been an avid outdoors woman and I spend a lot of time in these areas as well as the north island and this is something I’ve seen since I was a small child,” Sarrah Hanna told CHEK News. “Whatever we’re doing isn’t working and I’m here because I want to be a part of the solution.”

Chris Hillsden brought his own mini excavator in to do the work and a Bobcat was donated by Sunbelt Rentals. Regional Districts are also behind the cause, waiving all dumping fees for big cleanups like this one.

“So we’re able to dump at RDN (Regional District of Nanaimo) or other districts across the island without paying any fees. Last year the disposal costs reached $4000.00 that we didn’t have to pay,” Stuart said.

After a few hours Saturday the cleanup was done and they’re now just hoping they don’t have to go back for a third time next year.

]]> 1363195 Doctors call for Port Hardy to become a permanent overnight ER following death https://cheknews.ca/doctors-call-for-port-hardy-to-become-a-permanent-overnight-er-following-death-1363197/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 01:46:26 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363197

After a woman's death at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday, doctors are proposing to turn the ER department into a permanent overnight site.

The post Doctors call for Port Hardy to become a permanent overnight ER following death appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

After a woman’s death at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday, doctors are proposing to turn the ER department into a permanent overnight site.

Since 2023, Port Hardy residents have dealt with the harsh reality that their only emergency room within 40 kilometres closes every night from 5 p.m. to 7 a.m.

The ongoing overnight closures are a result of staffing shortages, according to Island Health.

On Thursday night, a woman arrived at the hospital after 5 p.m., when the ER was closed. At 5:11 p.m., BCEHS says paramedics learned of the patient’s presence and began treating her in the parking lot.

Eventually, she was brought inside to be treated by staff but was later pronounced dead.

“We’ve grown numb to this; it’s terrible. It’s terrible that it takes a tragic outcome, a death, to shake us from our numbness,” said Dr. Alex Nataros.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Nataros is the founder of the North Island Community Health Centre and has long criticized Island Health’s handling of the staffing shortage at the hospital. His colleague was involved in the attempts to save the woman’s life.

He sees this death as related to the ongoing closures.

“We’ve had over 30 walk-in patients today, and a number have raised concerns,” said Naratos.

“Having organizations like Island Health, full of managers and ‘Yes’ men, that agree to work and don’t improve the underlying problems leads to unnecessary deaths. I can count the deaths, and it’s terrible. Change is urgently needed.”

On Saturday, Island Health had no new update, referring CHEK News to information provided on Friday.

“We are reviewing the circumstances of this case with BC Emergency Health Services and it would be inappropriate to speculate on any factors that may have contributed while that review is underway,” said the health authority on Friday.

“What we can say at this time, based on initial review and follow-up, is that both Island Health care providers and BCEHS paramedics responded and provided emergency interventions.”

The ongoing overnight closures are sparking calls from North Island doctors to turn the Port Hardy ER into a permanent overnight regional emergency department. Naratos shared a letter to CHEK News that he says doctors have signed on to.

The letter says the Port McNeill hospital, roughly 43 kilometres from Port Hardy, has disproportionately taken on the burden for overnight ER coverage. Despite investments for the region, the ongoing staffing shortage continues to prevent the ER from opening 24/7, according to the letter.

“It has become clear to the local physicians that the safest and most sustainable long-term solution is to designate a single ER as the overnight site for the region permanently,” reads the letter.

Doctors want Port Hardy to become that site because of population size, patient volume, and acuity of calls.

“It’s a much sicker population, we’re also nearly double the size, and we have three First Nation reserves adjacent,” said Naratos.

He’s calling on the newly elected B.C. Government to take action for a situation that has long been dire.

Naratos says he spoke with North Island MLA Anna Kindy on Saturday.

“We spoke for over 20 minutes, and she gave me a clear commitment that her first job Monday morning is to get on the phone with Premier Lorne Doerkson and turn this ship around.”

“My heart goes out to the family and loved ones of the woman who died after arriving at Port Hardy Hospital on Thursday night, and to the paramedics, doctors and staff who fought to save her,” said MLA Anna Kindy in a statement.

“Minutes matter in an emergency, and our government is deeply committed to strengthening those services for people in every part of our province.”

Health Minister Ryan Peterson tells CHEK News in a statement that access to health care is a top priority and that he will work with all parties to ensure the findings of the review into the woman’s death lead to more reliable emergency care.

With files from CHEK’s Kori Sidaway

The post Doctors call for Port Hardy to become a permanent overnight ER following death appeared first on CHEK.

]]> 1363197 Island pipe fitter turned designer makes his runway debut at Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week’s closing night https://cheknews.ca/island-pipe-fitter-turned-designer-makes-his-runway-debut-at-vancouver-indigenous-fashion-weeks-closing-night-1363191/ Sun, 22 Nov 2026 00:47:33 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363191

After spending two decades in the oil fields, the Cree designer of Nanaimo says he's always been an artist, and tonight he gets to share his art at the final runway show of Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week 2026.

The post Island pipe fitter turned designer makes his runway debut at Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week’s closing night appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

After spending two decades in the oil fields, the Cree designer of Nanaimo says he’s always been an artist, and tonight he gets to share his art at the final runway show of Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week 2026.

Troy Armstrong is the owner and operator of Hat Felt Moments. He uses a mix of traditional craftsmanship with contemporary Indigenous designs to create fur felt hats and leather garments.

The Cree designer is from Saulteau First Nation, but has called Nanaimo home for the past 12 years.

Growing up, he spent a lot of time making art. His mother taught him how to sew.

“I’ve always been an artist in the back of my mind,” said Armstrong.

Then in his teenage years when they moved to a farm, and he also learned a lot from his grandma in terms of sewing and work ethic. And while art was an important part of his life, he was focused on building a financially secure future, and that led him to the oil fields where he worked as a pipe fitter for 20 years. 

Things changed drastically six years ago, when he had a brain aneurysm.

“It changed my whole view completely, as in it wasn’t all about money anymore,” said Armstrong.

“I had just kept on working all the time but I had to step back and realize that my family, my kids are getting older, and just take the time at home and do something I’m really passionate about.”

This shifted his focus about art as well.

First, he bought a hat company and started making hats in Nanaimo. Things took off quickly, his hats were being requested for photo shoots. Then he started making garments. And the response from the community, the youth, his family, was overwhelming.

“It was a whole different feeling I’d never felt before. And then I thought maybe this might be something I want to pursue. And that was like a year ago, actually.”

Just one year later, Armstrong now finds himself debuting his work on the runway of Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week. Arriving Wednesday for opening night, his nerves kicked in.

“So the first day I was overwhelmed by the fact that ‘oh I’m going to be on that stage,’ so I was kinda nervous at that point, but there’s so much love here. There’s so much support…you feel like family.”

Watch the video below of opening night’s Red Dress Night:

A few days later, he’s warmed up to the idea of being on that stage Saturday night.

Armstrong is one of six designers featured on the closing night. He’s showcasing his hats, jackets, pants and regalia, all with a western theme, a tip of the hat to his farm roots.

A Republican senator says a U.S. defence department’s memo that reportedly placed restrictions on co-operation with Canada applies to things such as participating in think-tank conferences, not military operations. 

Sen. Mike Rounds was responding to a Washington Post report on Friday that said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth penned the classified memo putting restrictions on military co-operation with Canada last week. The paper reportedly said it had not seen the memo and offered no detail on its contents. 

The senator said the memo does not affect any U.S. defence personnel in Canada today and does not impact the North American Aerospace Defence Command, North Atlantic Treaty Organization operations or the Five Eyes security alliance.

“It does limit general flag officer meetings to those that advance (defence department) objectives,” Rounds told reporters at the Halifax International Security Forum on Saturday.  “(U.S. defence officials) must request permission for Canadian think-tank events or social engagements. And it is OK to attend any 9/11 events.”

Rounds said he and a delegation of U.S. senators attending the Halifax conference had just attended a meeting with Canadian officials and shared the information with them. Defence Minister David McGuinty told reporters hours earlier he was unaware of the memo’s contents.

“After listening to this, (Canadian officials) said it sounds like it’s nothing new, nothing different than what they’ve been really practising under for the last year-and-a-half,” said the South Dakota senator. 

McGuinty said earlier in the day that it was “business as usual” between the Canadian and U.S. militaries and assured Canadians that co-operation between the two countries on defence, security and intelligence was continuing. 

“I’ve seen no evidence of (a change). I’ve checked with our top military folks, they’ve seen no evidence of change. We continue to co-operate. We continue to work together,” McGuinty told reporters.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a response to the story about the memo that the defence department is “taking steps to ensure its engagements with Canada advance tangible U.S. defense objectives and ultimately support a reinvigorated defense relationship.”

The statement, made late Friday, added that the department is prioritizing bilateral cooperation that strengthens the defence of the U.S. and “shared hemisphere” while also supporting Canada’s ability to meet NATO obligations. 

“This guidance does not impact defense intelligence cooperation, our binational NORAD command, or our cooperation through NATO,” Parnell said.

Several U.S. senators at the Halifax event acknowledged their country’s standing around the world has been impacted by the aggressive policies of U.S. President Donald Trump. 

Senator Tim Kaine, a Democrat, said the memo doesn’t help relations with Canada. He said he’s hopeful things will change when the new U.S. Congress takes office in January. Democrats took control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in this month’s midterm election.

“The tone is bad and it’s unnecessary,” said Kaine. “And we understand this actually goes back a ways and it is just the formalization of something that is now months and months old. I do think the new Congress is going to change the tone dramatically.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 21, 2026.

British Columbia’s official Opposition says the new Conservative cabinet is getting ready to tear down existing housing plans after eliminating the Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs as a separate office.

NDP interim leader Jennifer Whiteside says it is “deeply disappointing” to see the housing portfolio become part of the new Ministry of Local Government, Housing, Sport and Culture. 

She says the Conservatives’ decision appears to be the first step toward scrapping existing housing legislation.

The former B.C. labour minister says in a statement that housing affordability is a generational challenge and B.C. deserves a government that is “fighting to fix it, not one that abdicates its responsibility.” 

Premier Lorne Doerkson said at a news conference Friday that his government will be working with the federal government in “every way possible” to develop housing. 

He said that he committed himself to combining some of the ministries and the housing ministry is one of them.

Criticism also came from the B.C. Greens and their leader Emily Lowan.

Lowan said she is concerned about the signal that comes from combining the housing portfolio with others.

“British Columbians are struggling in an impossible affordability crisis, and in the worst housing crisis in a generation, this government has downgraded the housing portfolio, alongside labour,” she said.

Doerkson promised during and after the campaign to repeal key aspects of the provincial housing legislation introduced by the former NDP government of David Eby.

“We will return housing decisions to the people and the communities, who know their neighbourhoods so much better than Victoria,” he said during the inaugural meeting of the Conservative caucus after the election earlier this month.

Doerkson was referring to the repeal of Bill 44, which New Democrats considerer their signature piece of housing legislation.

The legislation legalized higher densities on single-lot properties in municipalities with populations above 5,000 people, but also came with housing targets, which local governments have criticized. 

The future of the legislation now falls within the responsibility of first-time legislator Cathie Ounsted, a former municipal councillor in Greater Victoria, who will head the new ministry following her appointment. 

Whiteside said in her statement that British Columbians also deserve a government that reflects B.C.’s diversity. 

“It is shocking that women make up just one-third of cabinet,” she said. “(For) the first time in three decades, B.C.’s Chinese-Canadian community, the province’s largest visible minority group with nearly 600,000 people, has no representation at the cabinet table.” 

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 21, 2026.

Warehouse workers in B.C. are celebrating after landing the first union deal for Amazon workers— not only in B.C., but also in Canada, and the first contract for Amazon workers across North America.

Unifor Local 114 says the new deal covers 800 warehouse workers at the Amazon YVR2 fulfilment centre in Delta.

An independent arbitrator made this happen, according to Amazon and the union, after the terms of the binding collective agreement came through on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.

The new agreement brings wages up to $29 per hour by the end of the three-year agreement. It includes severance protections of up to 18 weeks, an extra week of paid vacation for workers with 10 years of service, a Women’s Advocate, a grocery benefit, stat holiday scheduling based on seniority and improved employee benefits, including ergonomic protections to combat the physical demands of the job.

“Amazon told everyone a union contract would never happen, but workers proved them wrong,” said Unifor national president Lana Payne. “These workers stood up to one of the most powerful companies on earth and won rights in writing that Amazon cannot take away. Their courage won the day.”

Union representatives and workers say it’s taken a lot of work to reach the deal before any celebrations took place on Friday.

READ MORE: Amazon, workers ordered by B.C.’s labour board to reach deal via binding arbitration

In July 2025, the B.C. Labour Relations Board certified Unifor Local 114 as a union for Amazon workers after the retail giant hired extra workers to block the workers’ attempts to organize a union. On August 4, 2026, the Board ordered binding arbitration, ruling Amazon’s actions had interfered with reaching an agreement.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

The union plans to expand the collective agreement to more locations.

“This is a great victory for Amazon workers everywhere, not just in British Columbia but all across the world really we’ve been getting congratulations from everywhere. And it also extends to Vancouver Island as well because we’re opening up our hand to everyone to say lets join, lets make this collective agreement bigger and lets keep organizing,” Unifor’s western regional director Gavin McGarrigle told CHEK.

Whether the union plans to expand the agreement to warehouse workers on Vancouver Island, at the Amazon warehouse in Sidney or the exchange facility in Nanaimo, McGarrigle said the union is actively signing cards with warehouse workers across B.C., but would not comment on locations or future timelines.

Amazon is challenging the decision

Amazon is challenging the decision, criticizing the B.C. Labour Relations Board, saying the deal was achieved through an unfair process.

In a statement, Amazon says “an outside arbitrator imposed a collective agreement on our associates at YVR2, our fulfillment center in Delta, British Columbia, without giving associates the chance to ratify or vote on it.”

“Our associates weren’t allowed to vote on whether to accept it, which has become an unfortunate pattern with the British Columbia Labour Relations Board,” it adds.

Unifor’s western regional director Gavin McGarrigle says, “These Amazon workers now have the binding union contract they deserve and we intend to support them and thousands more improving their lives, in BC and elsewhere.”

The agreement runs until November 13, 2029.

Whether this new deal will expand to cover Amazon workers in other regions of B.C., including Vancouver Island, remains uncertain. Though the union says workers at other Amazon sites can talk to a Unifor organizer in confidence at organizing@unifor.org.

]]> 1363161 Ottawa says it lost $2M from emergency drug stockpile after freezer malfunction https://cheknews.ca/ottawa-says-it-lost-2m-from-emergency-drug-stockpile-after-freezer-malfunction-1363158/ Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:19:50 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1363158

The Public Health Agency of Canada has reported losing another $2 million in pharmaceuticals from the national emergency stockpile because of the mechanical failure of a freezer.

The post Ottawa says it lost $2M from emergency drug stockpile after freezer malfunction appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The Public Health Agency of Canada has reported losing another $2 million in pharmaceuticals from the national emergency stockpile because of the mechanical failure of a freezer.

The figure is in the annual federal public accounts published earlier this fall, and comes after the agency had to write off $20 million in pharmaceuticals from the stockpile a year earlier after another freezer malfunction.

The agency says the second loss involved a small portion of a specific drug treatment for responding to a biological threat.

“A mechanical failure prevented a freezer from maintaining its required temperature, which led to a small portion of a stockpiled drug treatment being exposed to temperatures outside the required storage requirements,” said Health Canada spokesperson Hélène-Annie Lavoie. “The affected products had to be disposed of as a result.”

Lavoie said the agency immediately launched an internal investigation and identified the cause of the problem.

She said the incident did not compromise Canada’s ability to respond to that potential threat, since the stockpile still had another treatment.

The official said she could not disclose the lost drug inventory for national security reasons. She said sharing that information could “expose sensitive operational details about how Canada prepares for and responds to chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or other public health threats.”

The agency says it has put in place new measures to prevent a recurrence.

The Canadian Press reported last year that an open freezer door caused the loss of medication worth $20 million at the national emergency stockpile in December 2024.

While officials again would not say exactly what was destroyed or how much, the agency said at the time it affected one type of therapeutic drug as a result of temperature fluctuations “caused by several factors.”

The Office of the Auditor General issued a report on the emergency stockpile in October which said the agency had written off more than $331 million in expired or damaged medical supplies. A spokesperson for the office confirmed both the $20 million loss and the $2 million loss, from the malfunctioning freezers, were included in that figure.

The national stockpile is a network of warehouses across the country where the government stores medical supplies, vaccines and emergency response equipment.

First established during the Cold War, the stockpile was initially intended to respond to a nuclear emergency.

Since then, it has been adapted to respond to outbreaks of diseases — including SARS and COVID-19 — natural disasters like hurricanes and floods, bioterror attacks and other emergencies.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 21, 2026.

Electric vehicle drivers have a new fast-charging option in Brentwood Bay, where half a dozen drivers can power up at the same time.

Installed at the Heritage School Museum, located at 7130 West Saanich Road, the station has three 180-kilowatt chargers, with room for six EVs to charge at once.

In 10 minutes, one 180-kilowatt charge provides vehicles with an additional 180 kilometres of driving. 

“Through power-sharing technology, each unit can serve two vehicles at once by splitting its output. For example, a 180-kilowatt charger can supply two vehicles with 90 kilowatts each. This allows up to six EVs to use the chargers simultaneously,” states BC Hydro in its release.

With the addition of the new Brentwood Bay station, BC Hydro has eight EV charging sites across Greater Victoria, amounting to a combined total of 57 charging ports for drivers.

In late September, BC Hydro announced a new fast-charging site in Esquimalt. The site features a similar arrangement, providing room for six, with three 180-kilowatt chargers.

Equipped with CCS, CHAdeMO and NACS connectors, the stations are able to power a wide range of electric vehicles.

The additional seven locations are listed below:

  • Sidney Beacon Plaza (2337 Beacon Avenue, Sidney)
  • Sidney Mary Winspear Centre (2304 Oakville Avenue, Sidney)
  • G.R. Pearkes Recreation Centre (3100 Tillicum Road, Saanich)
  • Saanich Plaza (3544 Blanshard Street, Saanich)
  • Victoria Downtown (1425 Store Street, Victoria)
  • Victoria Ogden Point Cruise Ship Terminals North and South (185 Dallas Road, Victoria)
  • Archie Browning Sports Centre (1151 Esquimalt Road, Esquimalt)

This summer, the province announced a $700 million plan to triple the number of charging ports across B.C. by 2035.

“BC Hydro’s public fast-charging network includes 917 charging ports at 190 locations in the province. As demand continues to grow, BC Hydro is accelerating expansion plans, targeting 3,500 ports by 2035,” stated the government release in July 2026.
